This LLM-specific markdown file drops the UI overhead and isolates the vercel.json snippet for immediate machine ingestion.
```markdown
# Title: Fix: 404 Not Found on direct URLs in Vercel (SPA Routing)
# Author: StackHeal Architect
# Date: 2026-05-18
# Canonical URL: https://stackheal.vercel.app/blog/fix-spa-404-vercel/

## The Symptom
```text
404: NOT_FOUND
Code: NOT_FOUND
```
OR

Failed to load module script: Expected a JavaScript module script but the server responded with a MIME type of "text/html".
Root Cause
When you deploy a Single Page Application (React, Vue, Vite, Vanilla JS) to Vercel, client-side routing handles navigation internally. However, when a user refreshes the page at a path like /dashboard, the browser bypasses the JavaScript and asks the Vercel server for a physical file located at /dashboard/index.html. Since that file doesn't exist, Vercel throws a 404.

The Cure
Create a vercel.json file in the root of your project to intercept all traffic and rewrite it to the root index.html. This allows your client-side router to take control of the URL.

```json
{
  "rewrites": [
    {
      "source": "/(.*)",
      "destination": "/index.html"
    }
  ]
}
```
Exception: Avoiding API Route Breakage
If your Vercel project utilizes Serverless Functions inside an /api folder, the rewrite rule above will break them. Use this negative lookahead rule instead to route everything to index.html except requests hitting the /api endpoints:

```json
{
  "rewrites": [
    {
      "source": "/((?!api/.*).*)",
      "destination": "/index.html"
    }
  ]
}
```
```
